data.description:
## Description
**What**: When the persisted marker class is db, the dso:task-decomposer always emits a rollback (down-migration) task and a rollback-verification task, authored in the same plan as the forward migration, with the rollback classified by destructiveness.
**Why**: Every schema migration ships with a classified, schema-state-verified rollback, so unsafe migrations are caught at plan time.
**Scope**:
- IN: db-class emission of the rollback + rollback-verification pair, classification, and schema-state assertion.
- OUT: sweep pairs; feature-flag pairs; sprint scheduling order.

## Done Definitions
- For a migration-class:db change, task-decomposer always emits a rollback task and a rollback-verification task authored in the same plan as the forward migration
  ← Satisfies: sc-3  (sc-3: db rollback pair emission)
- The rollback task is classified safe-revert for additive changes or compensating-forward for destructive changes, with ambiguous cases defaulting to compensating-forward and the task leading with a DATA LOSS RISK note
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- The rollback-verification task's done-definition asserts the resulting schema state rather than merely that the rollback task ran
  ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
  ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations
- [Maintainability] Shares the dso:task-decomposer emission surface with the sweep and feature-flag stories — add a db case to the single marker-class dispatch point; reserve the rollback / rollback-verification task-type namespaces.

## Escalation Policy
**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a planner, I emit a paired rollback plus rollback-verification task for db-class migrations
